newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 posts eight month low, falls below 500.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 posts eight month low, falls below 500.

text.p: The PX50 index on the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) slipped below 500 for the first time since mid-April on Friday falling 2.8 points to 498.4.
The RPIX also moved lower, dropping seven points to 1,020, putting the index just nine points above its all time low of 1,011.
Dealers said the breaching of the 500 barrier had been expected and doubted that it would do much to further dampen investor confidence.
"It isn't any break point being under 500. I don't see it as so important," said Ivan Kusacek a trader at Zivnostenska Banka in Prague.

The Czech equities market has been depressed for several months partly because of growing dissatisfaction with the regulatory framework of the bourse and partly because of increased hesitancy from foreign investors concerning the region as a whole.
Kusacek said he did not expect a revival in the Czech bourse's fortunes before Christmas.
"I just don't see anything to dramatically turn the market before Christmas," he said.
On the PX50 the major issues were all down.

Komercni Banka, which has outperformed the index in the last week, lost 40 crowns to 2,080, SPT Telecom fell five crowns to 2,860, CEZ dropped five to 955 and Ceska Sporitelna moved one crown lower to 326.
